interpretation: A (40,000/day) and B (122,500/day) are different quantities. A is an opening-period forecast; B is a market-share target that, under the stated peaking assumption, would load the peak direction to roughly 61-123% of the 10,000 pphpd design capacity. B is therefore best read as a mature, capacity-constrained upper case, not an opening-year figure. For the Bukit Chagar stress test, peak flow is capped by line capacity (10,000 pphpd) regardless of which daily figure is right.

stage1_planning_bounds_daily.basis: low = slower ramp-up (assumption A-011); base = official opening forecast; high = 2x official, about the level where base peaking reaches ~50% of capacity; mature_upper = claim B. Not a forecast; replaced by the frozen Stage 5 range.
